greek.meaning: guide; originally a slave who escorted boys to school and supervised their conduct; later teacher or educator
greek.forms: Singular: Nom παιδαγωγός, Gen παιδαγωγοῦ, Dat παιδαγωγῷ, Acc παιδαγωγόν
greek.etymology: From παῖς (PICE) 'child' + ἄγω (AH-go) 'to lead'. English descendants: pedagogy (teaching methods), pedagogue (teacher/educator), pedagogical (relating to teaching), demagogue (leader who appeals to prejudices, from δῆμος + ἄγω)
greek.usage_example: τὸν παιδαγωγὸν δεῖ τῶν παίδων ἐπιμελεῖσθαι — The guide must take care of the children
greek.did_you_know: The παιδαγωγός (pie-dah-go-GOHS) was often a foreign slave, considered unfit for physical labor but educated enough to teach. They carried a staff and had authority to discipline their charges in public, making them both servant and authority figure.
